rulings.text: Jameed is a liquid (owner ruling 2026-11-06). One form is used: «güneşe bırakılıp (cam kavanozlarda) bekletilmiş misket limonu suyu» / lomi suyu. Verbal: «suyu güneşe bırakır ve cam kavanozlarda bekletir». Heading: «güneşe bırakılıp bekletilen». Description: «güneşe bırakıp bekleterek». «güneşte bekletilmiş» is rejected because it collides with the second «bekletilmiş» («güneşte bekletilip … bekletilmiş») and merges the two steps the source keeps apart (set in the sun, aged in jars). «güneşe bırakmak» names the setting-out step without implying drying. Never «güneşte kurutulup / kurutur / kurutulan» for the juice.

Dried lime stays: «kurutulmuş meyve / kurutulmuş lomi» (lomi-body) and «budama, güneşte kurutma ve bekletme» (history-72 craft list, per brief). These are about the fruit and are never confused with cemid (BL2-cemid-r2).

blind_disposition.why: «bekletmek» is the normal verb for ageing/keeping food. The description keeps the same verb as the gloss.

blind_disposition.flag: [2] whether jars sit in the sun or juice is sunned first; duration
blind_disposition.why: The Arabic authority is silent on this (cf. ru JF-5), so it is not fixable in translation.

blind_disposition.flag: [5] three uses blur cemid vs dried lime
blind_disposition.why: Lomi is the named subject, and dried fruit is said explicitly («kurutulmuş meyve olarak»). The reader's answer (b) separates them correctly.

blind_disposition.flag: [6] «güneşte kurutma» object unstated, clashes with cemid
blind_disposition.why: The brief keeps the craft list. It is the fruit's craft, and the source list is equally bare. The cemid gloss in the same sentence now says «güneşe bırakılıp bekletilmiş … suyu».

out_of_scope: «Öyleyse iki vahaya ne kalıyor?» / «Bir köken iddiasından» antecedents (context lost in extraction)
«Kutlama o kadar büyüdü ki» no antecedent; «bunun en görünür biçimi cemiddir» stilted; comma splice «… lomi suyu, bütün yıl kullanılır»
«El-Ahsa Geliştirme Kurumu» body name; «… âdeti de vardır» wordy
